grh_cc47754b5ee6642eec94.title: Billy D. Burton
paragraphs: Gifted jazz trumpeter Billy D. Burton repeatedly sabotages a brilliant career through heroin, erratic performances and an inability to accept the demands placed on him. Friends, lovers and manager Doris keep trying to pull him back while critic Leo Leather chronicles both the flashes of genius and the disasters, including missed concerts, an aborted European tour and behavior that steadily destroys Billy's professional standing. Billy marries a woman who shares his drug use, later enters a six-month rehabilitation program, but relapses almost immediately and continues losing work. Near the end of his life he spends several weeks away from the public pressure, practicing seriously and reaching a new maturity in his playing. Before he can make the comeback others are waiting for, he dies after a sudden attack, leaving those who heard his final work convinced that he had at last begun to find himself in his music.

grh_ccca25220c8b4173543c.title: American Family Robinson
paragraphs: Affluent businessman John Robinson sells his company and suburban home and moves his wife, children and elderly father to an isolated island in hopes of rebuilding the family life that success has hollowed out. Most of the family embraces the adventure, but teenage Brad resents losing his friends and comforts and remains determined to leave. The Robinsons repair an old house, build a new home, plant a garden and learn the dangers of the island, while John's father forms a bond with Brad. A volcanic eruption suddenly tears through their new life, destroying much of the work they have done. Brad risks himself to help his grandfather and promises to rebuild the ruined garden, then realizes he no longer wants to be sent away. The disaster breaks down the hostility between father and son, and the family decides to remain together on the island and begin again.

grh_cc66ff709dc79034f910.title: Aunt Emma
paragraphs: After her husband dies and her children leave home, Britt's Aunt Emma comes to Powder Creek convinced that both she and her wandering nephew need a household to run. Britt tries to adapt to domestic life but quickly realizes he is miserable being fussed over and cannot abandon the range. Local storekeeper Ethan is fond of Emma but stays back because he thinks she is sacrificing herself for Britt, so Britt announces he is leaving and pushes Ethan to propose. Emma accepts, revealing that she had already recognized Britt could never be domesticated and that Ethan is exactly the sort of man who enjoys being looked after.
